title: Basic Steps to Run the Machine

steps.title: 1. Turn On Breaker
steps.description:
Step 1. Turn on Breaker
There are 5 AOL machines.
This is AOL 1. It's larger than AOL machines 2, 3, 4, and 5.
The remaining AOL machines are smaller than AOL 1.
The breaker boxes are located on the back wall behind the Kuntai work area. There are two to the right of the air compressor and one to the left.
NOTE: Breakers are not turned off as a regular closing function. The Breakers are typically already turned on. If the breakers are already turned on, then move to step 2.
The breaker box on the left contains AOL 1's circuit breaker switches.
These are the switches for AOL 1. They're in the "on" position.
The breaker box on the right contains the circuit breaker switches for the remaining AOL machines 4 and 5.
Both sets of switches are in the "on" position.
The circuit breaker switches for AOL machines 2 and 3 are located in this breaker box.
The two sets of switches are in the "on" position.
For safety purposes, only authorized personnel may activate the circuit breaker.

steps.title: 2. Power On the Machine
steps.description:
Step 2: Turn on the machine.
The emergency-stop button is depressed, which means the machine is turned off.
Turn on the machine by turning the emergency-stop button clockwise until the button pops up.
The screen should turn on.
Press the upper left part of the screen to unlock the screen.

steps.title: 3. Program Calibration
steps.description:
Step 3: Program Calibration
Press the "origin" button after every start-up. The purpose of the origin is to calibrate the machine on its "0 , 0" position.
You should see "start go origin" displayed on the screen.
You should see the machine calibrating on its own.
The screens should say "origin succeed" if nothing failed.
If the origin calibration failed, STOP CALL WAIT.
Important: Whenever you press "origin," it erases the loaded file. You must load the file again. See step 6.

steps.title: 4. Material Setup (Fabric)
steps.description:
Step 4: Material Setup (Fabric)
Identify the material to be used.
Find the information on the work order.
You can also find it on the Part Specification Sheet (PSS).
Locate the correct material in the storage area.
Use a hand truck to move the material roll from the storage area to the material roll stand behind the AOL machine.
Return hand truck to storage location.
Put bubble wrap on the floor next to the material roll, and then push the roll onto the bubble wrap.
Take the label holder and the base, and put them in the storage area.
Put the base here with the others. These are continuously re-used.
Put the label holder here with the others. They are not discarded. They are continuously re-used.
Place the label sleeve with the material label here.
Unload the used material roll core from the material roll stand.
Put the used core in the storage area with other cores.
Loading the new roll requires two people. Ask a production team lead or another machine operator for help.
Move the bubble wrap back under the material roll stand.
The wooden guide goes against the roll stand on the left side.
The material will line up all the way to the left side of the roll stand.
The right side of the material will lock in place with a metal ring.
There will be some gap between the locking ring and the roll stand. This will vary depending on how much of the paper core is sticking out.
Another locking ring may be used against the inside of the roll stand holder to increase stability.
There should be no space between the roll of material and the right-side wooden guide.
Remove the bubble wrap from the material roll. Return it to the storage area.
Remove the tape from the material roll.
The roll should unroll from the "under" position.
With help from a production team lead or another machine operator, pull the end of the material under the lower roll on the stand and set the material on the conveyor belt.
Feeding the fabric material under the lower bar on the roll stand will help eliminate wrinkles.
If you're not sure if release paper is on the bottom or top, ask the production team lead.
Origin should be finished at this time. Move the bar to the back and press clamp. Then navigate the bar to the desired position.

steps.title: 4. Material Setup (Carpet)
steps.description:
Step 4: Material Setup (Carpet)
Carpet materials must be fed straight onto the belt or on a slight downward angle. If the material is on an upper angle, the material will wrinkle before cutting.
Here, the carpet is fed onto the belt at a very slight downward angle. This will help avoid wrinkling the material before cutting.
Here, the carpet is being fed at an upper angle. This will cause material wrinkling before cutting.
Use the yellow roll stand to get the material higher.

steps.title: 5. Set Zero Position
steps.description:
Step 5: Set Zero Position
Make sure that the middle of the laser pointer is within 10 mm from the material edge.
Peel back a small portion of the paper to make sure there's adhesive present under the laser position.
If you are satisfied with the position, press "set zero" on the "work" screen to lock in the starting point.
Press the "set zero" button to lock in the position. Then, press the " [] " button to confirm the cutting area on the material.
After pressing the " [] " button, make sure the cutting area stays inside the adhesive area of the material. Reset the "zero position" if the laser moves outside of the adhesive area.
Use this guide only if there are both red and black lines present on the release paper side of the material.

steps.title: 6. Choose File
steps.description:
Step 6: Choose File (AOL 2-5 Only)
On the touchscreen, go to the "test" page by pressing the "test" button.
Press the "SD" button or the "USB" button, depending on the part to be cut.
Locate the part to be cut. Then, press the pink "read" button to the left of the part number and name. Next, press the "down arrow" button.
A drawing should appear. Press the refresh button and wait 10 seconds.
Here is the same process, but pressing the "USB" button on the "test" screen.
Step 6: Choose File (AOL 1 Only)
AOL 1 uses a laptop to load the programs to the machine.
Locate the laptop for this machine.
Turn the computer on.
Enter the PIN: 6 3 3 0 6 3 3 0.
Locate the "Xiao" program icon.
Double-click on the icon to open the program.
The "Xiao" program is now running.
Check the work order to confirm the part information.
Select "OPEN" in the top left corner.
Find the correct program.
Double-click the file to open it.
Check the shape of the part and confirm that it's the correct one for this work order.
You can confirm the shape by checking the Part Specification Sheet (PSS).
If the shape on the computer doesn't match what's shown on the PSS, or if you have any questions or concerns at all, ask a production team lead for help.
After confirming the shape, locate and click once on the "send 1 2" button.
This will send the program to the AOL machine.
After sending the program to the machine, confirm on the machine panel that the transfer was successful. You should see this message: "Receive Complete"

steps.title: 7. AOL 2-5: Set "rolldist" Number
steps.description:
Step 7: Set rolldist number (AOL 2-5 Only)
"Rolldist" (short for "roll distance") means how far the machine will move the material after each completed cycle.
This is the previous cycle of six pieces. The pieces have already been removed by the machine operator.
This is the cutting area of the current cycle that is about to finish.
The "roll distance" is how far forward this cycle's cut pieces will be moved at the end of the cycle.
Go to the "test" menu by pressing the "test" button on the touchscreen.
Select "SD" or "USB," depending on the part.
The "roll distance" number should be at the end of the filename.
Here, it's 580.
Take note of this number: 580.
Go to the "speed" menu by pressing the "speed" button.
Locate the "rolldist" box.
Set the "rolldist" number by pressing this box here.
Use the keypad to enter the roll distance number you found at the end of the file name on the "test" menu page.
Step 7: Set roll add number (AOL 1 Only)

steps.title: 7. AOL 1: "Set "roll add" Number
steps.description:
Step 7: Set Roll Add Number (AOL 1 Only)
Roll add adds or subtracts from the designated amount of movement with the program to ensure the next cut does not create miscuts and does not waste material yield.
Go back to the laptop. Check the Xiao file name. Look for the roll add number.
This is the file name.
Take note of this number, including the + symbol.
This is the roll add number.
Press the "speed" button to go to the speed screen.
The roll add box already contains the correct roll add number for this part: + (positive) 10. If there's a different number in the box, STOP CALL WAIT.

steps.title: 8. Confirm Work Area
steps.description:
Step 8: Confirm Work Area
Move to the "work" screen by pressing the "work" button on the touchscreen.
On the "work" screen, confirm the work area by pressing the "[ ]" button.
After pressing the "[ ]" button, the machine will travel in the path shown.
Make sure to confirm the whole path is within the cutting boundaries.
You should be able to see black boundary lines on both sides of the release paper side of the material roll.
When confirming the work area, this red laser cross should stay within the boundary lines.
If the laser cross moves outside of the boundary lines, then that means the machine will cut parts outside of the adhesive area.
There is no adhesive in this area. Cut parts that include this area won't have adhesive, so they would be non-conforming.
There is a thin line of adhesive here.
Then there's a thin area without adhesive before the main adhesive area begins as you move inward.
The main adhesive area begins here and continues to the other side of the release paper on the opposite side of the machine.
When you press the "[ ]" to confirm the work area, the red laser cross must stay in the main adhesive area.
For parts cut on AOL machines 2, 3, 4, and 5, the area 10 millimeters inside the edge of the paper does not have adhesive.
There's no adhesive here.
Make sure that the work area stays between the black lines, without also including the black lines.

steps.title: 9. First Off Inspection
steps.description:
Step 9: First-Off Inspection
Go to the work screen by pressing the "work" button.
Press the "repeat" button for a single cycle.
Check full cut cycle of parts.
AOLs 2 and 3 and AOLs 4 and 5 are operated as a pair. Each pair of machines is operated by one machine operator. Stage one full cut cycle of parts from each machine together for the first-off inspection.
This stack of parts is from the machine to the left of this machine.
This stack of parts is from this machine.
In addition to the parts to be inspected, put the wooden inspection pick and the inspection guide card near the parts for the inspector.
The inspection guide card will be hanging from the inspection workstation.
Move the card to where the quality inspector will inspect the first-off parts.
Locate the inspection pick and place it with the parts to be inspected.
Use the radio to call for a first-off inspector. Say "First-off, AOL."
An inspector will come and check the parts.
Each piece will be inspected to the standards listed on the Part Specification Sheet (P S S).

steps.title: 10. Run Production
steps.description:
Step 10: Ready for Production
If you need to pause production for breaks or issues in the process, press the "pause" button on the work screen.
When you need to resume production after pressing the "pause" button, press the "continue" button.

steps.title: 11. Last Off Inspection
steps.description:
Step 11: Last-Off Inspection
Go to the "work" screen by pressing the "work" button.
Press the "repeat" button for a single cycle.
Check full cycle of cut parts.
Stage the parts to be inspected and the inspection tools neatly for the inspector.
Use the radio to call for an inspector. Say "Last Off, AOL."
The inspection must be done by a trained First-Off/Last-Off inspector, not the machine operator.
Inspect each piece to the standards listed on the Part Specification Sheet (PSS).

steps.title: 12. Shutdown and Closing Work
steps.description:
Step 12: Shutdown and Closing Work
Once production is complete, press the red emergency-stop button to turn off the machine.
Finish recording any information on the work order.
5-S the area, including discarding of any scrap material. There's a garbage chute in the back of the warehouse between the two bay doors.
